text: Our group project is due this weekend and the GPU cluster queue has been stuck for hours, so none of my runs are even starting.
label: No physio
response: That's frustrating. When a project deadline is looming, waiting for a long queue can make the whole process feel much longer than it actually is. It's understandable that you're feeling frustrated, especially since you've already invested time in preparing your code.

text: I keep refreshing the queue every ten minutes instead of studying for my other courses, and I know it is not helping.
label: No physio
response: That's a very common pattern when we're waiting for something important. It's easy to get caught up in the habit of checking the queue every few minutes, even though we know it's not helping us learn. Instead of trying to control the waiting time, try setting a timer for 20-30 minutes and challenge yourself to stay focused on your studies during that time.

text: I have barely slept this week and I am starting to make small mistakes in my code that I would never normally make.
label: No physio
response: That's a clear sign that you're pushing yourself too hard. When we're exhausted, our brain doesn't have the energy to focus, and even small mistakes become much more likely. It's not a sign of weakness—it's a sign that you need to give yourself permission to rest.

text: Part of me feels like if this does not work out, all the effort I put in this semester was for nothing.
label: No physio
response: That fear is understandable. When we invest so much time and energy into something, it's natural to wonder whether it was worth it. But it's important to remember that every experience, whether it leads to a fulfilling career or not, has taught you something valuable. Even if this path doesn't work out, you'll have gained skills, confidence, and a clearer idea of what you want. That's something to hold onto, not just because it's true, but because it gives you hope for the future.

text: I told a friend about it and they said I am overthinking, but it does not feel that simple to me.
label: No physio
response: That sounds like a difficult conversation to have. When someone tells us to stop overthinking, it can feel dismissive of our own feelings. It's understandable that you're still feeling uncertain. Sometimes overthinking isn't just about thinking too much—it's about trying to make sense of something that feels unclear.

text: I think I need to accept that some of this is out of my control and focus on what I can actually finish.
label: No physio
response: That's a very realistic and compassionate thing to say. When we're feeling overwhelmed, it's easy to lose sight of what's truly within our power. By focusing on what you can control—your own effort and attitude—you'll be able to make steady progress even when the situation itself seems uncertain.

text: Thanks, I feel a bit calmer now. I am going to sleep tonight and look at it fresh tomorrow.
label: No physio
response: That sounds like a good plan. Sometimes taking a break from a difficult decision helps us approach it with a clearer mind the next day. You don't have to make this decision tonight—just give yourself permission to sleep on it and come back to it with a fresh perspective tomorrow.
